meta.title: AI Sovereignty Scan — Oneview Logic
meta.description: Assess your organisation's EU AI Act, GDPR and data-sovereignty risk per AI tool and account tier.

hero.eyebrow: EU AI Act · GDPR · Data sovereignty
hero.title: How sovereign is your AI use?
hero.subtitle: In about 10 minutes, map the AI tools your organisation uses and get an indicative risk score per tool and account tier. You also get a branded report with a prioritised action plan.
points: Covers {tools} AI products and account tiers

usecases.title: Use cases
usecases.intro: What is AI used for in your organisation? Select everything that applies. Each use case maps to an EU AI Act risk category.

recruitment_hr.label: Recruitment / HR screening
recruitment_hr.hint: CV screening, candidate ranking, interview analysis

employee_monitoring.label: Employee monitoring / performance evaluation
employee_monitoring.hint: Productivity scoring, task allocation, promotion or termination decisions

credit_insurance.label: Credit or insurance scoring
credit_insurance.hint: Creditworthiness, pricing of life or health insurance

biometric_identification.label: Biometric identification or categorisation
biometric_identification.hint: Face or fingerprint recognition, categorising people by biometric traits

emotion_recognition.label: Emotion recognition of employees or students

critical_infrastructure.label: Critical infrastructure
critical_infrastructure.hint: Safety components in energy, water, traffic or digital infrastructure

customer_chatbot.label: Customer-facing chatbot
customer_chatbot.hint: Customers or citizens interact directly with AI

external_content.label: AI-generated content published externally
external_content.hint: Marketing texts, images, video, news or public information

stop_prohibited.title: Stop or re-assess prohibited AI use immediately
stop_prohibited.detail: Pause {useCases} and get legal advice. Art. 5 prohibitions have applied since 2 February 2025.

discontinue_cn.title: Stop using China-based AI services for company data
discontinue_cn.detail: Block {tools} and move users to an approved alternative. If needed, run open-weight models on EU infrastructure instead.

stop_shadow_ai.title: End shadow AI: provide an approved alternative
stop_shadow_ai.detail: Offer an approved business tier and block personal accounts for {tools}. Tell employees which tools are allowed.

upgrade_business_tier.title: Move personal and free accounts to business or enterprise tiers
upgrade_business_tier.detail: Replace consumer accounts of {tools} with business or enterprise plans that come with a DPA and admin controls.

disable_training.title: Switch off model training on your data
disable_training.detail: Turn off training in the settings of {tools}, or move to a tier that never trains on customer data.

art50_transparency.title: Implement AI Act transparency (Art. 50)
art50_transparency.detail: Tell people when they interact with AI and label AI-generated content ({useCases}). This has applied since {date}; marking for older generative systems applies from {date2}.

sign_dpas.title: Sign data processing agreements with every AI vendor
sign_dpas.detail: Sign a GDPR Art. 28 DPA with each vendor. Tools without a DPA: {tools}.

ai_policy.title: Adopt an AI usage policy
ai_policy.detail: Set out which tools are allowed, for which purposes and with which data, and who approves new tools.

do_dpia.title: Carry out a DPIA for AI processing of personal data
do_dpia.detail: A DPIA (GDPR Art. 35) is expected when AI processes personal data at scale or supports decisions about people.

enable_eu_residency.title: Enable EU data residency where available
enable_eu_residency.detail: Switch on EU storage and processing for {tools}. For Microsoft 365 Copilot, also switch off flex routing.

prepare_high_risk.title: Prepare for AI Act high-risk obligations
prepare_high_risk.detail: For {useCases}: set up human oversight, logging, instructions for use, worker information and supplier checks before {date}.

ai_literacy.title: Run an AI literacy programme
ai_literacy.detail: Art. 4 requires measures that support AI literacy for staff who use AI. The Omnibus made this an obligation of effort; it did not remove it.

ai_register.title: Set up a register of AI systems
ai_register.detail: Record each tool, tier, owner, purpose, data categories, DPA and risk category. This also supports your GDPR records of processing.

sovereign_alternative.title: Use a sovereign alternative for sensitive workloads
sovereign_alternative.detail: Consider an EU provider, or open-weight models on EU infrastructure, for sensitive data now handled by {tools}.

assess_dpo.title: Check whether you need a Data Protection Officer
assess_dpo.detail: A DPO is mandatory for large-scale monitoring or special-category processing, and advisable for systematic AI processing.

human_oversight.title: Define human oversight for AI-supported decisions
human_oversight.detail: Decide who reviews AI output before it affects people, and how to escalate or override it.

report.title: AI Sovereignty Scan
report.generated_by: Generated by Oneview Logic's AI Sovereignty Scan
report.omnibus_changes: What the Digital Omnibus on AI changed

sme.1-9: Micro-enterprise: if your turnover is within SME limits, AI Act fines are capped at the lower of the fixed amount and the percentage of turnover, and SME support measures apply.
sme.10-49: Small enterprise: if your turnover is within SME limits, AI Act fines are capped at the lower amount, and SME support (e.g. priority sandbox access) applies.
sme.50-249: Medium-sized enterprise: SME relief applies if your turnover or balance sheet is within SME limits (lower fine cap, simplified documentation).
sme.250-999: Not an SME. Under the Omnibus you may qualify as a small mid-cap (fewer than 750 employees, turnover ≤ €150m or balance sheet ≤ €129m), which gives partial relief.
sme.1000+: Large enterprise: the full fine regime applies (the higher of the fixed amount and the percentage of worldwide turnover).

report.alternatives_intro: For each tool scoring High or Critical: estimated score after switching, assuming EU residency is enabled and use is company-approved.
report.no_alternatives: No tool scored High or Critical, or no lower-risk alternative is known.

checklist.dpas: Data processing agreements with AI vendors
checklist.tools_transfer_gap: Tools without a verified transfer mechanism: {tools}

report.methodology_text: Each tool × tier gets four sub-scores (0–100, higher is riskier): data sovereignty (30%), GDPR compliance (30%), EU AI Act exposure (25%) and security & contract (15%). Modifiers are then added for free or personal tiers used with sensitive data, shadow AI, and special-category or employee data (capped at +35). The organisation score is the usage-weighted tool average (80%) blended with the governance score (20%). It is never lower than 80% of the riskiest high-exposure tool. Knowledge-base facts that could not be verified, and "don't know" answers, are scored as the riskier option. A prohibited use case always gives a Critical result.
report.sources_intro: Facts verified on {date}. Every fact in the knowledge base has a source and a verification date.
report.unverified_intro: Facts marked unverified for your tools (scored conservatively):
report.disclaimer: This is an indicative self-assessment, not legal advice. Results depend on your answers and on publicly available vendor information that can change at any time. Have the conclusions reviewed by a qualified adviser before relying on them.
